name: Brinzolamide
mechanism: Inhibits carbonic anhydrase in ciliary processes of eye, reducing aqueous humor production and intraocular pressure
dosing: One drop in affected eye(s) twice daily. If used with other eye drops, space at least 5 minutes apart
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to sulfonamides, severe renal impairment (CrCl <30ml/min), hyperchloraemic acidosis
interactions: Oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (avoid concurrent use - ↑ systemic side effects), high-dose aspirin (theoretical interaction)
monitoring: IOP monitoring. Check for signs of systemic absorption in patients with renal/hepatic impairment. Electrolytes if concerned about acidosis
pregnancy: Avoid - no adequate data. Systemic carbonic anhydrase inhibitors are teratogenic in animals
sideEffects: Bitter/unusual taste (common), blurred vision, local irritation, conjunctivitis, dry eye, rarely systemic effects (headache, fatigue) or hypersensitivity
pharmacokinetics: Topical administration, some systemic absorption, binds to carbonic anhydrase in RBCs, half-life: 111 days in RBCs (after repeat dosing)
clinicalPearls: Second/third-line for glaucoma when prostaglandin analogues/beta-blockers insufficient or contraindicated. Warn about bitter taste (common complaint). Can combine with prostaglandin analogues or beta-blockers. Less systemic side effects than oral acetazolamide
indication: Open-angle glaucoma, ocular hypertension (adjunct or when prostaglandin analogues/beta-blockers contraindicated)
